tools.name: list_connections
tools.description: List configured connection profiles (never includes passwords).

tools.name: list_databases
tools.description: List databases available for a connection profile.

params.name: connectionId
params.description: Name of a configured connection profile, as returned by list_connections. Defaults to the active connection.

tools.name: list_schemas
tools.description: List non-system schemas in the currently selected database.

tools.name: list_objects
tools.description: List objects (tables, views, …) in a schema.

params.name: connectionId
params.description: Optional connection profile override — does not change session context.

params.name: database
params.description: Database to use instead of the current one, on connectionId or the active connection.

params.name: include_partitions
params.description: When true, list child partition tables individually. Default false groups partitioned parents.

params.name: kind
params.description: Filter by object kind: "table", "view", or "materialized_view".

params.name: schema
params.description: Schema name to list, e.g. "public". Defaults to all non-system schemas.

tools.name: get_current_context
tools.description: Return the active profile, database, and access mode.

tools.name: switch_connection
tools.description: Switch the session to another connection profile / database.

params.name: connectionId
params.description: Name of a configured connection profile, as returned by list_connections. Defaults to the active connection, so passing only `database` switches database.

params.name: database
params.description: Database name on that connection. Defaults to the profile's configured database.

tools.name: run_select
tools.description: Run a read-only SELECT or WITH query. DML/DDL are rejected. Supports parameterized execution via `params` ($1, $2, …). Returns up to 50 rows by default; has_more says whether more exist, and total_count is included when the whole result fits (or with count: true).

params.name: connectionId
params.description: Optional connection profile override — does not change session context.

params.name: count
params.description: When true and has_more is true, also return total_count. Runs the query a second time, so only ask when the total matters.

params.name: database
params.description: Database to use instead of the current one, on connectionId or the active connection.

params.name: format
params.description: Output format: "compact" (default columnar), "json", "markdown", or "csv".

params.name: limit
params.description: Maximum rows to return. Defaults to 50; capped by profile max_rows.

params.name: params
params.description: Bound parameters for $1, $2, … in `sql`. JSON values: string, number, boolean, or null.

params.name: resolve_fks
params.description: When true, add __resolved suffix columns for foreign-key IDs in the result.

params.name: sql
params.description: A single SELECT or WITH statement, schema-qualify table names where possible.

params.name: timeout_ms
params.description: Per-query statement timeout in milliseconds; capped by profile statement_timeout_ms.

tools.name: explain_query
tools.description: Run EXPLAIN (no ANALYZE execute) for a SELECT/WITH query.

params.name: connectionId
params.description: Optional connection profile override — does not change session context.

params.name: database
params.description: Database to use instead of the current one, on connectionId or the active connection.

params.name: sql
params.description: A single SELECT or WITH statement to explain (not executed).

tools.name: discover_tools
tools.description: Dynamically discover and inspect specialized MCP database tools by keyword query (e.g., 'locks', 'bloat', 'index') or category ('query', 'dba', 'write'). Use this when you need specialized tools beyond the core surface.

params.name: category
params.description: Restrict to a tool category: "query", "dba", "meta", or "write".

params.name: query
params.description: Free-text keyword to search tool names/descriptions, e.g. "locks" or "bloat".

tools.name: run_doctor
tools.description: Run diagnostic health checks on active database connection, permissions, session guards, and index status.

tools.name: add_database
tools.description: Connect another Postgres database for this session and save it as a read-only profile, without the password passing through the chat. Give the connection details; this opens a one-time page on the user's computer where they check those details and type the password themselves. Never ask the user to paste a password into the chat, and never put one in a shell command or file. Tell the user what the page is for, then call again with setupId to see whether they finished.

params.name: dbname
params.description: Database name.

params.name: host
params.description: Database server hostname.

params.name: name
params.description: Name for the new connection, e.g. "billing". Must not already be in use.

params.name: port
params.description: Database server port (default 5432).

params.name: setupId
params.description: Check on a setup started by an earlier call instead of starting a new one.

params.name: sslmode
params.description: libpq sslmode, e.g. "require" or "verify-full".

params.name: url
params.description: postgres:// URL without a password, as an alternative to host/port/dbname/user.

params.name: user
params.description: Database role to log in as.

tools.name: setup_connection
tools.description: Automatically detect or configure a database connection. Scans environment variables, workspace files, and local settings, eliciting missing credentials when supported.

params.name: dbname
params.description: Database name to connect to.

params.name: host
params.description: Database server hostname.

params.name: interactive
params.description: Prompt (elicit) for missing credentials instead of failing. Default false.

params.name: name
params.description: Profile name to assign/detect.

params.name: password
params.description: Database role password. Never written to disk in plaintext — stored in the OS keyring, or the call fails with the password_command/password_file alternative.

params.name: port
params.description: Database server port (default 5432).

params.name: sslmode
params.description: libpq sslmode value, e.g. "disable", "require", "verify-full".

params.name: url
params.description: Full postgres:// connection URL; if given, host/port/dbname/user/password are ignored.

params.name: user
params.description: Database role/username.

tools.name: save_profile
tools.description: Save or update a database connection profile in user configuration with atomic backup and dynamic session reload. Merges into the existing named profile by default — omitted fields are preserved, not cleared. Pass replace: true to wholesale-replace instead.

params.name: access_mode
params.description: Session access mode: "read", "write", or "admin". Setting "write" or "admin" requires confirm_elevated_access: true, or the call is rejected.

params.name: confirm_elevated_access
params.description: Required (must be true) when access_mode is "write" or "admin" — explicit opt-in for a privilege escalation. No effect when access_mode is omitted or "read".

params.name: dbname
params.description: Database name to connect to.

params.name: host
params.description: Database server hostname.

params.name: max_rows
params.description: Row cap applied to run_select/export_query for this profile.

params.name: name
params.description: Profile name to save under.

params.name: password
params.description: Database role password. Never written to disk in plaintext — stored in the OS keyring, or the call fails with the password_command/password_file alternative.

params.name: port
params.description: Database server port (default 5432).

params.name: replace
params.description: If true, replace the profile wholesale instead of merging with existing saved fields. Default false.

params.name: sslmode
params.description: libpq sslmode value, e.g. "disable", "require", "verify-full".

params.name: url
params.description: Full postgres:// connection URL; if given, host/port/dbname/user/password are ignored.

params.name: user
params.description: Database role/username.

tools.name: test_profile
tools.description: Test a database connection profile or inline parameters and return server version, superuser status, and round-trip latency.

params.name: dbname
params.description: Database name (inline test).

params.name: host
params.description: Database server hostname (inline test).

params.name: name
params.description: Existing profile name to test. Omit to test inline parameters instead.

params.name: password
params.description: Database role password (inline test).

params.name: port
params.description: Database server port (inline test).

params.name: sslmode
params.description: libpq sslmode value (inline test), e.g. "require".

params.name: url
params.description: Full postgres:// connection URL to test inline (alternative to name).

params.name: user
params.description: Database role/username (inline test).

tools.name: export_profile
tools.description: Export a secret-sanitized TOML configuration for team sharing (.nexql/config.toml) with all passwords and credentials stripped.

params.name: format
params.description: Output format, currently only "toml" is supported (default).

tools.name: import_profile
tools.description: Import a team configuration file (.nexql/config.toml) or TOML content into local user configuration.

params.name: content
params.description: Raw TOML content to import. Provide this or `path`, not both.

params.name: path
params.description: Filesystem path to a .nexql/config.toml file to import.

tools.name: resolve_target
tools.description: Autonomously find which connection/database matches a user's hint (a database name, environment, host fragment) and/or an object hint (a table/view name), searching across ALL configured connections and their indexed schemas. Use it when the request names a database, environment, or object outside the current session context. When the match is unambiguous it switches the session context automatically and returns the resolved connection/database; only returns `ambiguous: true` with a candidate list when multiple equally-plausible matches exist, in which case surface those candidates to the user rather than guessing.

params.name: hint
params.description: Free-text hint about the target connection: database name, environment, or host fragment.

params.name: objectHint
params.description: Free-text hint about a table/view name expected to live in the target database.

tools.name: orient
tools.description: Compact overview of the whole database: tables and views with columns, primary key and row estimate, foreign-key joins, and enum values. Use it for broad questions ("what's in this database?"); for a specific question, search_schema is cheaper.

params.name: focus
params.description: Substring to filter tables/joins by ref (e.g. "orders"). Omit to summarize the whole indexed schema.

tools.name: inspect_or_search
tools.description: Composite schema discovery: search by keywords and return matching objects with columns, keys, and row estimates in one call — replaces search_schema → describe_object chains.

params.name: include_columns
params.description: Include per-column definitions in each match. Default true.

params.name: limit_objects
params.description: Maximum matching objects to return. Default 3.

params.name: query
params.description: Natural-language or keyword search, e.g. "cash card".

tools.name: search_all_databases
tools.description: Cross-database schema search: find which connection/database owns a table or view across every configured profile and every database it can connect to. Databases without a schema index are indexed on first search. Query a hit with run_select's `database` argument.

params.name: limit_connections
params.description: Max connection/database pairs to search. Default 20.

params.name: limit_per_database
params.description: Max hits per connection/database pair. Default 3.

params.name: query
params.description: Table/view name or keyword to search across all connections and databases.

tools.name: search_schema
tools.description: Search the live, auto-indexed database schema using natural language or keywords to find tables, views, materialized views, and functions matching the query. Start here before writing SQL, then describe_object the tables you will use — do not assume a table exists without finding it here.

params.name: query
params.description: Natural-language or keyword search, e.g. "customer email".

tools.name: describe_object
tools.description: Get structural details of a specific database object (table, view, or materialized view) including columns, data types, constraints, and indexes.

params.name: connectionId
params.description: Optional connection profile override — does not change session context.

params.name: database
params.description: Database to use instead of the current one, on connectionId or the active connection.

params.name: resolve_refs
params.description: When true, attach enum values and resolved FK label samples on columns.

params.name: resolve_refs_limit
params.description: Max distinct FK values to resolve per column when resolve_refs is true. Default 20.

params.name: table
params.description: Table, view, or materialized view as "schema.name" (e.g. "public.customers"); a bare name is resolved if unambiguous.

tools.name: get_join_path
tools.description: Find the shortest path of join relationships and foreign keys between two database tables.

params.name: from
params.description: Start table as "schema.name" (e.g. "public.orders"); a bare name is resolved if unambiguous.

params.name: to
params.description: End table as "schema.name" (e.g. "public.customers"); a bare name is resolved if unambiguous.

tools.name: sample_values
tools.description: Retrieve a list of sample values from a specific table column to inspect its contents. Only works on read-only SELECT queries.

params.name: column
params.description: Column of `table` to sample values from.

params.name: table
params.description: Table or view as "schema.name" (e.g. "public.orders"); a bare name is resolved if unambiguous.

tools.name: rebuild_index
tools.description: Rebuild the schema index for the active database connection.

params.name: depth
params.description: Index scope: "shallow" (structure only) or "full" (structure + sample values). Default "full".

tools.name: refresh_index
tools.description: Refresh the schema index for the active database connection using previous build scope.

tools.name: get_ddl
tools.description: Get the DDL / definition of a database object. Views, materialized views, functions, and indexes return their CREATE statement; tables return structured DDL (columns, constraints, indexes).

params.name: connectionId
params.description: Optional connection profile override — does not change session context.

params.name: database
params.description: Database to use instead of the current one, on connectionId or the active connection.

params.name: kind
params.description: Object kind hint: "table", "view", "materialized_view", "function", or "index". Auto-detected if omitted.

params.name: object
params.description: Object as "schema.name" (e.g. "public.orders"); a bare name is resolved if unambiguous.

tools.name: table_stats
tools.description: Get size, row-count, activity (scans, inserts/updates/deletes, dead tuples, vacuum/analyze times) and per-column statistics for a specific table.

params.name: connectionId
params.description: Optional connection profile override — does not change session context.

params.name: database
params.description: Database to use instead of the current one, on connectionId or the active connection.

params.name: table
params.description: Table as "schema.name" (e.g. "public.orders"); a bare name is resolved if unambiguous.

tools.name: index_usage
tools.description: Get index usage statistics (scan counts, size, definition, type) for a specific table's indexes. Useful for finding unused or missing indexes.

params.name: table
params.description: Table as "schema.name" (e.g. "public.orders").

tools.name: list_running_queries
tools.description: List currently executing (non-idle) queries in the connected database with pid, user, state, wait events, and duration.

tools.name: find_blocking_locks
tools.description: Find lock contention: which queries are blocked waiting on locks and which pids/queries are blocking them.

tools.name: slow_queries
tools.description: List the slowest statements by mean execution time from pg_stat_statements (requires the extension; returns a hint if not installed).

params.name: limit
params.description: Maximum number of statements to return. Default 10.

tools.name: db_health_check
tools.description: Run a database health overview: size/connection stats, cache hit ratio, tables with dead tuples needing vacuum, active connections, and blocking-lock count. Sections that fail are reported individually; partial results are still returned.

tools.name: get_index_status
tools.description: Return schema-index status for the active connection/database: indexed_at, fingerprint, object counts, and optional live fingerprint drift. Returns status:"missing" (not an error) if no index has been built yet.

tools.name: list_extensions
tools.description: List installed PostgreSQL extensions (name, version, schema).

tools.name: server_settings
tools.description: Return key PostgreSQL server settings from pg_settings (memory, connections, timeouts, autovacuum, version).

tools.name: suggest_indexes
tools.description: Suggest indexes from high sequential-scan tables, unindexed FK columns, and optional pg_stat_statements / EXPLAIN plan heuristics. Pass sql to analyze a specific query plan.

params.name: limit
params.description: Maximum number of suggestions to return. Default 10.

params.name: sql
params.description: Optional SELECT/WITH statement whose plan should inform the suggestions.

tools.name: find_unused_indexes
tools.description: List indexes with idx_scan = 0 (never used since stats reset), excluding primary keys, unique indexes, and constraint-backed indexes.

params.name: limit
params.description: Maximum number of indexes to return. Default 10.

tools.name: bloat_report
tools.description: Approximate table bloat via dead-tuple ratio from pg_stat_user_tables (simplified estimate — not physical page bloat). Tables with >1000 dead tuples, ordered by bloat %.

params.name: limit
params.description: Maximum number of tables to return. Default 10.

tools.name: find_missing_fks
tools.description: Find likely missing foreign keys: prefers schema-index join-graph inferred edges; falls back to catalog naming (*_id columns without an FK matching a PK).

params.name: limit
params.description: Maximum number of candidates to return. Default 20.

tools.name: export_query
tools.description: Run a read-only SELECT/WITH and format results as CSV, JSON, or SQL INSERT statements. Honors max-row / max-char caps. For sqlinsert, pass table as schema.name.

params.name: format
params.description: Output format: "csv", "json", or "sqlinsert". Default "csv".

params.name: sql
params.description: A single SELECT or WITH statement to run and export.

params.name: table
params.description: Target table as "schema.name", required when format="sqlinsert".

tools.name: list_roles
tools.description: List PostgreSQL roles (attributes). Pass role to get memberships and table privileges for one role.

params.name: role
params.description: Specific role name to inspect memberships/privileges for. Omit to list all roles.

tools.name: db_dashboard
tools.description: One-shot live metrics bundle: DB size/owner, connection-state breakdown, top tables by size, object counts, active queries, and blocking locks. Soft-fails per section.

tools.name: deep_plan_analysis
tools.description: Run EXPLAIN (ANALYZE by default) and return parsed plan metrics (scan counts, bottlenecks, buffer stats) plus severity-graded findings: estimate skew, expensive function/CTE/subquery nodes, and recommendations. Set analyze=false for plan-only (no execution). The single query-plan-analysis tool — covers what separate explain_analyze/analyze_query_plan tools used to.

params.name: analyze
params.description: If false, use plan-only estimates without executing the query. Default true.

params.name: sql
params.description: A single SELECT or WITH statement to analyze.

tools.name: schema_diff
tools.description: Compare two schemas in the current database (or sourceSchema vs targetSchema). Returns structured table/column/constraint/index diffs. Read-only — does not apply changes.

params.name: sourceSchema
params.description: Name of the schema to treat as the baseline, e.g. "public".

params.name: targetSchema
params.description: Name of the schema to diff against the baseline, e.g. "staging".

tools.name: generate_migration
tools.description: Emit migration SQL to evolve sourceSchema toward targetSchema (from a live schema_diff). Read-only — returns SQL text, never executes it. Destructive drops are commented out.

params.name: sourceSchema
params.description: Name of the schema to migrate from, e.g. "public".

params.name: targetSchema
params.description: Name of the schema to migrate towards, e.g. "staging".

tools.name: auto_tune_query
tools.description: Autonomous query tuner: executes EXPLAIN ANALYZE, checks table statistics, evaluates missing indexes, and outputs step-by-step performance tuning recommendations.

params.name: sql
params.description: A single SELECT or WITH statement to tune. It executes for real.

tools.name: check_ddl_safety
tools.description: Safety guard for migration DDL: inspects SQL for dangerous exclusive locks (e.g. non-concurrent index builds, column drops, table rewrites) and outputs risk scores and safe zero-downtime alternatives.

params.name: ddl
params.description: One or more DDL statements to inspect for locking risk. Not executed.

tools.name: execute_sql
tools.description: Execute DML (and DDL in admin mode) inside an explicit transaction. Set dry_run=true to roll back after execution. Errors always roll back.

params.name: dry_run
params.description: If true, execute then roll back so no change persists. Default false.

params.name: include_diff
params.description: When true (default when dry_run), capture before/after row snapshots for UPDATE/DELETE.

params.name: sql
params.description: A single DML statement (INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE), or DDL if the session is in admin mode.

params.name: timeout_ms
params.description: Override statement_timeout for this call, in milliseconds. Unlike run_select, may exceed the profile's configured ceiling — useful for bulk INSERT/DDL. Bounded by NEXQL_MCP_MAX_TIMEOUT_MS.

tools.name: edit_row
tools.description: Structured insert, update, or delete by primary key. The server builds parameterized SQL — pass table (schema.name), action, values, and pk for update/delete.

params.name: action
params.description: Operation to perform: "insert", "update", or "delete".

params.name: dry_run
params.description: If true, execute then roll back so no change persists. Default false.

params.name: include_diff
params.description: When true (default when dry_run), capture before/after row snapshots for update/delete.

params.name: pk
params.description: Primary-key column name/value pairs identifying the row. Required for update/delete.

params.name: table
params.description: Target table as "schema.name".

params.name: values
params.description: Column name/value pairs to insert or update. Required for insert/update.

tools.name: import_data
tools.description: Batch INSERT rows from a JSON array of objects into a table. Optional columns array fixes column order; otherwise keys from the first row are used.

params.name: columns
params.description: Explicit column order to insert with. Defaults to the keys of the first row.

params.name: rows
params.description: Array of row objects, each mapping column name to value.

params.name: table
params.description: Target table as "schema.name".

tools.name: apply_ddl
tools.description: Apply a DDL statement (CREATE, ALTER, DROP, TRUNCATE, …) in admin mode inside a transaction. Set dry_run=true to roll back. Scope: objects within the connected database only — CREATE DATABASE / DROP DATABASE are always rejected, in every access mode.

params.name: confirm_destructive
params.description: Required (true) when the statement is classified CRITICAL risk by check_ddl_safety's rules (e.g. DROP TABLE, TRUNCATE), unless the client supports MCP elicitation — in that case the server asks the human directly instead of requiring this argument. Call check_ddl_safety first, or dry_run:true to preview. Not required when dry_run is true. Default false.

params.name: dry_run
params.description: If true, execute then roll back so no change persists. Default false.

params.name: sql
params.description: A single DDL statement to apply.

params.name: timeout_ms
params.description: Override statement_timeout for this call, in milliseconds. Unlike run_select, may exceed the profile's configured ceiling — useful for bulk INSERT/DDL. Bounded by NEXQL_MCP_MAX_TIMEOUT_MS.

tools.name: create_index_concurrently
tools.description: Run CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY outside a transaction (non-blocking index build). Admin mode only.

params.name: sql
params.description: A single CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY statement.

tools.name: run_maintenance
tools.description: Run VACUUM, ANALYZE, or REINDEX outside a transaction. Admin mode only. Optional table (schema.name); vacuum supports full=true.

params.name: action
params.description: Maintenance action: "vacuum", "analyze", or "reindex".

params.name: full
params.description: For action="vacuum", run VACUUM FULL (rewrites the table, takes an exclusive lock). Default false.

params.name: table
params.description: Target table as "schema.name". Omit to run against the whole database where supported.

tools.name: terminate_query
tools.description: Cancel (pg_cancel_backend) or force-terminate (pg_terminate_backend) a backend by pid. Admin mode only. Refuses superuser targets and the current session.

params.name: force
params.description: If true, force-terminate the backend (pg_terminate_backend) instead of a soft cancel. Default false.

params.name: pid
params.description: Backend process id to cancel/terminate.

prompts.description: Run a full database health assessment and summarize issues by severity.
prompts.name: health-check

prompts.description: Find the slowest queries and propose index or rewrite improvements.
prompts.name: analyze-slow-queries

prompts.description: Explore and summarize the database schema around a topic.
prompts.name: explore-schema

prompts.description: Diagnose lock contention and identify the root blocking session.
prompts.name: debug-blocking

arguments.description: The schema change to implement, e.g. "add soft-delete to orders".
arguments.name: change

prompts.description: Draft a safe PostgreSQL migration for a described schema change.
prompts.name: write-migration

prompts.description: Compare two PostgreSQL schemas and summarize structural differences.
prompts.name: diff-schemas

prompts.description: Deep-analyze a query plan with severity-graded findings.
prompts.name: plan-deep-dive

prompts.description: Analyze a table's indexes, bloat signals, and access patterns; propose improvements.
prompts.name: optimize-table

arguments.description: The SQL SELECT (or other read query) to explain.
arguments.name: sql

prompts.description: Explain a SQL query against the live schema and propose plan improvements.
prompts.name: explain-this-query
